text: This final lesson ties together every chapter of this course, the six courses beneath it, and the full seven-course arc Alderbrook Wealth Partners' incident just ran end to end, from detection through a closed, hunted, and reported case. It closes by naming, specifically, what a graduate of this entire stage is now ready for in a real SOC.

Chapter 1's NIST lifecycle named every phase this case moved through. Chapter 2's plan and RACI meant the on-call analyst knew exactly what to check and who to call. Chapter 3's triage and scoping discipline turned one sign-in alert into a two-entity, confirmed incident. Chapter 4's evidence-safe order protected what Lesson 30's forensics needed.

Chapter 5's judgment call sent a persisted host to rebuild instead of live cleanup, validated before returning to production. Chapter 6's after-action report paired every finding with an owner and a date. Chapter 7's hypothesis-driven hunt found a second compromised account the original alert never caught. Chapter 8 is all seven, run together, because that's the only way any of them were ever meant to work.

None of it works without six courses underneath: how IT teams escalate work, networking and cybersecurity fundamentals, Windows and Linux security, endpoint detection, SOC and SIEM fundamentals, and Sentinel's own analytics rules and investigation graph. This course is where all six of those become one incident, handled start to finish.

Triaging a real alert, scoping past the one entity it names, containing without destroying evidence, finding and removing actual root cause, validating before production, writing an owned after-action report, and hunting for what the SIEM missed — that is the working toolkit of a Junior SOC Analyst or Cybersecurity Analyst, demonstrated, not just claimed.

That's the Job-Ready Foundation stage complete — seven courses, from how a SOC actually works through networking, system hardening, threat detection, SIEM operations, Sentinel, and now a full incident handled end to end. Next up: Advanced Specialization, starting with Security Engineering, IAM & System Hardening.
